subject: Future Tech
title: O'Neill Cylinders and Space Habitats
description: A micro-lesson that makes O'Neill Cylinders and Space Habitats usable.

hook.text: In 1976, physicist Gerard O'Neill proposed giant rotating cylinders in space where millions of people could live.

buildup.text: Each cylinder would spin to create gravity on its inner surface. Windows would let in sunlight for farms and parks.

discovery.text: O'Neill calculated that asteroid materials could build habitats supporting far more people than any planet's surface.

twist.text: Jeff Bezos champions this idea. Blue Origin's long-term vision is millions of people living in orbital colonies.

climax.text: Building an O'Neill cylinder requires space mining, manufacturing, and transport at a scale we can't yet achieve.

punchline.text: Why settle a planet when you can build a world?

quiz.question: Who proposed the concept of O'Neill cylinders?
